title: Charles Borromeo (1538–1584)
hook: a rich reforming bishop who stayed in Milan through the plague

segments.voice: Yesterday, Philip Neri, half a beard and a room full of songs. Your line was holy joy. Today, a very different saint: serious, thin, and stubborn about one thing.

Plague in Milan. Shops shut, streets empty, carts collecting the dead. Those who can afford to leave the city are leaving, and some of the officials go with them. One carriage is going the other way. The archbishop, who had been away, comes back in. He's from a wealthy, powerful family, and the nephew of a pope. He could have stayed safely away. Instead he walks the streets, visits the sick, and organizes food and care. His name is Charles Borromeo.
screen: `PLAGUE IN MILAN.` → `THE RICH ARE LEAVING.` → `ONE CARRIAGE COMES BACK.`

segments.voice: First, the privilege. Charles was made a cardinal very young, because his uncle was the pope: exactly the kind of favoritism reformers complained about. Instead of enjoying it, he worked hard in Rome to help bring the Council of Trent to its close. Second, the reform. The council told bishops to live in their own dioceses and care for their people. That sounds obvious, but it answered a real problem: bishops who lived far away and simply drew the income. Charles moved to Milan and stayed. He visited parishes, opened seminaries to train priests, and pared down his own household. Not everyone loved him for it. Some resisted his reforms, and one group even tried to have him killed. Third, the plague. When the sickness came, he stayed and served. Tradition says he gave away his own goods, even his household hangings, to clothe the poor, and led processions of prayer through the city barefoot. Fourth, the shepherd. Some readers see in him Jesus's words in John, in the Douay-Rheims: "I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd giveth his life for his sheep." In the same chapter Jesus describes the hired hand who sees the wolf coming and runs. The difference, the chapter suggests, isn't courage. It's whose sheep they are. Charles treated Milan as his own. The rich young cardinal is remembered for something simple. He stayed.
screen: `A CARDINAL BY FAVORITISM.` · `REFORM: LIVE WITH YOUR PEOPLE.` · `THE PLAGUE, AND THE BARE FEET.` · `THE SHEPHERD AND THE HIRED HAND.` · then, large: `THE GOOD SHEPHERD GIVETH HIS LIFE.`

segments.voice: Think of a place, a person or a task you'd like to escape right now, and just notice the pull to leave, without deciding anything big. Then ask whether there's one small way to stay a little longer, with care. If you pray, ask for the strength to stay; if you don't, just breathe, and stay with the question.
Charles Borromeo. The reforming archbishop of Milan, a pope's nephew from a rich family who lived with his people and stayed with them through the plague.
Your line: he stayed. Milan was his own, so he didn't run. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Catholics honor Charles Borromeo as a patron of bishops, seminarians and catechists, and seminaries named for him still train priests.

chat.says: Charles Borromeo was a pope's nephew. Why is he a saint and not a scandal?
options: He got his rank by favoritism, but he lived among his people and stayed with Milan through plague.
He refused the cardinal's rank and lived as a poor hermit outside Milan instead.
He spent his life in Rome, so Trent's rule for bishops never applied to him.
chat.meaning: Made a cardinal through favoritism, Charles moved to Milan, reformed it, and when plague came he came back in and stayed.

notes: Claims rule: no dates or ages in the voice ('very young' for his cardinalate). The absent-bishop problem is stated only as what Trent's residence decree addresses; confirm.
He was away from Milan (at Lodi) when plague broke out and returned: standard account; confirm. 'Some of the officials go with them' refers to the governor's departure; confirm.
Giving away household hangings to clothe the poor, and barefoot processions: attributed to tradition. Confirm.
The attempted assassination (by members of the Humiliati) is mentioned without detail; confirm wording.
'His Milan became a pattern other bishops studied' (trapdoor) is a historians' judgment; confirm or soften.
